title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: MCP-based agents for US Government clouds
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, general agent entitlements and blocking controls are supported. It accurately reports conflicting government-cloud documentation and distinguishes general guidance from unconfirmed details of this enablement.

claims.claim: The roadmap introduces MCP-based agents in Microsoft 365 Copilot for US Government clouds.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): MCP-Based Agent Enablement for U.S. Government Clouds

claims.claim: Learn does not separately describe this roadmap item's government-cloud enablement.
claims.quote: Searched: "564607" "MCP"; "Microsoft 365 Copilot" "MCP" "government" "default" rollout. Opened build-mcp-plugins, overview-plugins, known-issues, overview-declarative-agent and the Copilot service description; no item-specific explanation.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: MCP plugins are custom actions for declarative agents.
claims.quote: MCP and API plugins are custom actions that enable declarative agents in Microsoft 365 Copilot to interact with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers or REST APIs

claims.claim: The plugin manifest connects a declarative agent to a remote MCP server.
claims.quote: The plugin manifest connects the agent to a remote MCP server

claims.claim: The agent plugin does not package or host the running MCP server.
claims.quote: it doesn't package or host the running server.

claims.claim: MCP declarative-agent actions dynamically resolve their tools from the MCP server at runtime by default.
claims.quote: For plugins based on an MCP server, Copilot resolves the plugin's tools dynamically at runtime by default, directly from the MCP server.

claims.claim: A developer can instead pin a fixed tool set.
claims.quote: When building the agent, a developer can optionally pin a fixed set of tools in the plugin manifest instead.

claims.claim: The Copilot service description lists declarative agents as not currently available in DoD.
claims.quote:
| Feature | Commercial/Worldwide | GCC | GCCH | DoD |
| Declarative agents | Yes | Yes | Yes^8^ | Not currently available |

claims.claim: The service description limits GCC High declarative agents to Agent Builder and agents published through admin controls.
claims.quote: GCC-High currently only supports declarative agents created using Agent Builder and those published via admin controls.

claims.claim: The declarative-agent overview instead gives DoD limited support for pro-code agents built with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit.
claims.quote: Department of Defense (DoD): Limited support - only pro-code agents built with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit are supported.

claims.claim: The declarative-agent overview supports both Agents Toolkit pro-code agents and Agent Builder in GCCH.
claims.quote: Government Community Cloud High (GCCH): Pro-code agents built with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit are supported. Agent Builder is also now available in GCCH.

claims.quote:

claims.claim: Agents invoke available MCP tools subject to tool configuration, authentication and permissions.
claims.quote: A plugin doesn't grant a user access to data that the user or component isn't otherwise authorized to access.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated this government-cloud enablement's default state on arrival, so defaultState is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft 365 Copilot" "MCP" "government" "default" rollout; "MCP" "government" "tenant" "switch". Read roadmap, build-mcp-plugins, known-issues and management guidance; none specifies this enablement's arrival default.

claims.claim: No source states that this enablement changes existing users' behaviour.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft 365 Copilot" "MCP" "government" "default" rollout; "564607" "MCP". Read roadmap, MCP walkthrough, known-issues and declarative-agent overview; no existing-user behaviour change is specified.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: MCP tool calls go to a separately hosted server outside Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: The agent sends a request to the plugin's MCP server or API, which is hosted outside of Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Learn does not explain the relationship between this government-cloud feature's remote MCP server and the government cloud boundary.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft 365 Copilot" "MCP" "government" data boundary. Read overview-plugins and data-privacy-security; search also returned gov-overview. These distinguish external services and Copilot boundaries but do not describe this item's server boundary.

claims.claim: Learn says agents grounded in shared tenant work data are unavailable in GCC, GCCH and DoD.
claims.quote: Agents grounded in shared tenant work data aren't currently available in Microsoft 365 Government Community Cloud (GCC), Government Community Cloud High (GCCH), or Department of Defense (DoD) environments.

claims.claim: The MCP walkthrough uses OAuth to obtain an access token on behalf of the signed-in user for each server call.
claims.quote: Copilot then uses the registration to obtain an access token on behalf of the signed-in user each time the agent calls the MCP server.

claims.claim: The MCP apps page permits authentication type None for development.
claims.quote: If your MCP server is still in development and doesn't implement authentication, select None as the authentication type.

claims.claim: The MCP apps page instructs developers to add authentication before production deployment.
claims.quote: Add authentication before you deploy to production.

claims.claim: The Government restriction on authenticated custom actions covers authenticated MCP actions.
claims.quote:
The following features aren't currently supported in Microsoft 365 Government tenants:
- Authenticated custom actions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: MCP and API plugins can create, update and delete connected-system data when supported.
claims.quote: users can ask a declarative agent to query an MCP server or REST API for information and, when supported, create, update, and delete data and objects through natural language prompts.

claims.claim: Dynamic discovery can change the agent's available tools without republishing the agent.
claims.quote: Dynamic tool discovery means you get the latest tools the MCP server exposes without waiting for the agent to be repackaged and republished.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated item-specific rollout mechanics.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft 365 Copilot" "MCP" "government" "default" rollout; "564607" "MCP". Read roadmap, MCP walkthrough, government availability and known-issues guidance; no item-specific rollout sequence or mechanism.

claims.claim: Agents published by the organisation go through admin approval.
claims.quote: Before you make these agents available to members of your organization, these agents go through an admin approval to ensure compliance and readiness.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; After rollout
claims.claim: Agents can be reviewed under Agents > All agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote:
Select Agents > All agents.
In the All agents page, select an agent from the list of agents.

claims.claim: The block control is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block > Block agent > Save.
claims.quote:
Select Agents > All agents.
In the All agents page, select an agent from the list of agents.
In the agent details pane that opens, immediately under the agent's name, select Block or Unblock.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks the selected agent package.
claims.quote:
Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: Agent blocking targets the selected agent and does not necessarily block a shared MCP server or revoke connected-service permissions or credentials.
claims.quote: These actions apply to the selected agent. If the agent is included in a plugin, don't assume the action also applies to the whole plugin package, its skills, shared MCP servers, or connections. Agent approval or blocking doesn't necessarily grant or revoke connected-service permissions or credentials.

claims.claim: The general agent block control restricts use across the organisation using the same controls as other apps.
claims.quote: Block or unblock agents for the entire organization by using the same controls that work for any other app in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: The UI guidance has no equivalent explicit statement about blocking in DoD.
claims.quote: Searched: "site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365" "government" "MCP". Read agent-actions and manage-copilot-agents-integrated-apps: their government notes address GCCH/GCCM publishing, not DoD blocking.

claims.claim: No MCP-specific tenant switch or MCP server allow list is documented for this Microsoft 365 Copilot government-cloud declarative-agent feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "MCP" "GCC" "allow" "admin"; "MCP" "government" "tenant" "switch". Read manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers, agent-tools-overview, Agent 365 service description and manage-byo-mcp-server; BYO explicitly excludes Microsoft 365 Declarative Agents.

claims.where: Open questions: MCP server restrictions and Agent 365 controls
claims.claim: Applicability of Agent 365 server-management controls to this government-cloud declarative-agent scenario remains unsettled.
claims.quote: Searched: "site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365" "government" "MCP". Read Agent 365 service description (tool controls available in GCC), manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers (route-dependent enforcement), and manage-byo-mcp-server (Microsoft 365 Declarative Agents aren't supported).
